title: Namespaces and Visibility

# Namespaces and Visibility

Namespaces provide ownership, query context, lifecycle metadata, and the
authorization boundary for RECAP data.

## Hierarchical paths

Namespace paths use slash-separated segments:

```text
beamline
└── beamline/amx
    └── beamline/amx/proposal/312345
```

Paths are canonicalized before lookup. A namespace has one parent, a unique
path, mutable metadata, lifecycle status, and a revision. Ancestor metadata can
contribute effective context to a child namespace.

## Ownership

Provenance aggregates are namespace-owned:

- Process templates are identified by namespace, name, and version.
- Resource templates are identified by namespace, name, and version.
- Process runs are identified by namespace and name.
- Top-level resources use UUID identity; names may repeat across a namespace.

The namespace remains immutable for an aggregate after creation. Moving an
aggregate is not an ordinary update operation.

## Lifecycle

Namespace and provenance aggregate lifecycle follows forward-only transitions:

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-cap: "Forward-only RECAP lifecycle transitions"
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> MUTABLE
    MUTABLE --> ACTIVE
    MUTABLE --> ARCHIVED
    ACTIVE --> ARCHIVED
    ARCHIVED --> [*]
```

The diagram shows that records can move from mutable to active or archived, and
active records can move to archived; unavailable transitions have no arrows.
Same-state transitions are accepted. Archived records remain resolvable by
identity and historical relationships but are excluded from default discovery.
Templates and resources become immutable after stable references; changing an
immutable resource creates a derived copy.

## Query context

`RecapClient.namespace()` returns another `RecapClient` bound to one namespace
path. The scoped view shares connection state with its source client, so local
SQLite resources or authenticated remote transports are opened once and safely
remain available while either view is in use. Bracket access is an additive
alias for the same operation:

```python
namespace = client.namespace("beamline/amx")
same_namespace = client["beamline/amx"]
resources = namespace.query_maker().resources().all()
```

For remote work, scope the client directly when its lifetime matches one
namespace:

```python
with RecapClient.from_url("http://localhost:8000", api_key=API_KEY).namespace(
    "beamline/amx"
) as client:
    client.query_maker().resources().all()
```

The namespace path travels beside the serialized query specification. It is not
embedded in predicates, which allows the same query shape to work locally and
through the remote GraphQL read backend.
